full_judgment:
3. The present respondent Nos. 1 and 2, as petitioners, filed the above mentioned Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 2007 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for pre-emption. 

 9. Mr. Mahbubey Alam has mainly argued that the petitioners are not at all owners of any land contiguous to the land transferred, that there are sufficient evidence and materials on record to prove that there is a public road in between the land transferred and the land of the pre-emptors. The learned Counsel has contended that all the Courts below have failed to consider and evaluate these evidence and materials properly; the learned Advocate has stated also that in the trial Court, at the instance of this present petitioner, a local investigation was held by an Advocate Commissioner to find out whether there was any public road in between that land transferred and the land of the pre-emptors and that the Advocate Commissioner, after holding local investigation properly, submitted report stating clearly that there was a public road in between the land transferred and the land of the pre-emptors and that before the revisional Court a DP Parcha was filed which showed that there was a government road in between the land transferred and the land of the pre-emptors but the revisional Court inspire of this present petitioner's earnest prayer did not take that DP Parcha into consideration. Mr Mahbubey Alam has argued that the Advocate Commissioner's report and the DP Parcha filed before the revisional Court proved conclusively that there was a public road in between the land transferred and the land of the petitioner. The learned Advocate has contended that the findings and decision arrived at by the Courts below have been erroneous causing great injustice to this present petitioner and, as such, interference by this Division is necessary.
